deploy.on_merge: Merging puts nothing on the three sites. The frontends under apps/ are Cloudflare Pages direct uploads (agenttool-web behind the agenttool-proxy apex Worker, agenttool-docs, agenttool-dashboard); no workflow uploads them. A push to main runs .github/workflows/deploy-api.yml when it touches docs/** or api/**, and that deploys the API only when what the image bakes in (api/, docs/agenttool.jsonld, docs/kingdom-bundle.json, bin/stage-doctrine-docs.sh, the doctrine docs) differs between the live revision and main
deploy.after_deploy: Frontend release from clean GitHub main with `bin/deploy.sh --no-migrate --no-api` (docs/DEPLOY-PROCEDURE.md Phase 4; bin/frontend-deploy.sh is the lower-level uploader). Then the sampled frontend parity probes, a production page-policy sweep, and a live check of each served icon and card. HTML answers `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate, no-transform` (observed 2026-11-05); the zone's Browser Cache TTL must respect origin headers, or non-HTML files hold for 4 hours (DEPLOY-PROCEDURE.md)

notes: favicon.ico, closed in source 2026-11-10, live after the next frontend release: the served-surface guard (bin/served-surface-guard.ts; its test bin/tests/served-surface-guard.test.ts in CI, and bin/frontend-deploy.sh before any upload) reads PNG, SVG, ICO, text, fonts and archives, and refuses any other binary unless public/private-guard/served-surface.json names that exact file with a reason. Under the owner's decision of 2026-11-10 it reads an ICO only when every byte is accounted for (header, directory and images in directory order, with no gap, overlap or trailing byte) and each image is a non-interlaced PNG of at most 256 pixels a side, held stricter than a PNG file: only known chunks, each CRC right; every text field (keyword, language tag, translated keyword, text) read on its own with no NUL in it, compressed text one zlib stream that ends with its chunk; the pixel data inflated the same way to exactly the rows its header implies, and those rows read for text; an empty IEND that ends the image. The icon's bytes, text fields and pixel rows are read as Latin-1, UTF-8 and UTF-16. Pixel values, palette entries and colour-calibration chunks are image bytes the guard does not decode: it catches accidents and plain text, and does not claim to catch data someone hides in pixel values on purpose. Any other image type (a bitmap among them, which the guard refuses on its own too), a cursor and anything malformed are refused. So the kit's favicon.ico is in the three sites' upload set byte for byte, with no policy entry, and /favicon.ico stops answering 404 once a release uploads it. The pages still link favicon-32.png and favicon.svg (head-snippet.html); the ICO answers clients that ask for /favicon.ico without reading a page. JPEG stays unreadable, so the cards are PNG (cards.sh).

One look, three sites: agenttool.dev (apps/web), docs.agenttool.dev (apps/docs) and app.agenttool.dev (apps/dashboard) share apps/_shared/theme.css, so serve lists one target per site folder, each with the same icon files.

brand/ sits at the repository root, outside apps/. bin/frontend-deploy.sh uploads each apps/<site> folder and strips only CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and README.md, and apps/_shared is linked into every site as shared/, so a brand folder anywhere under apps/ would be published.

Release rules: a frontend release is an outward act and needs Yu's word for that release (AGENTS.md: a local edit request alone does not authorize publication or deployment). On this Mac, bin/deploy.sh needs Bun 1.3.5 exactly (memory note agenttool-ui-hearth-2026-10-17).

Heads: every page that drew the site's ring as a data-URI favicon now links the kit's icon files (favicon-32.png in place of favicon.ico) and its site's manifest (head-snippet.html). The scheme each declares is what it paints without JavaScript. The 17 agenttool.dev pages (apps/web/style.css has a prefers-color-scheme rule) and the four docs and app pages with data-layout="workspace" that load /shared/workspace.css (docs index, agents and roadmap; app index) carry color-scheme "light dark" and the theme-color pair #F7F3EC (light) and #141210 (dark). The other 43 docs and app pages paint paper unless mode.js runs (apps/_shared/theme.css has no prefers-color-scheme fallback), so they carry one theme-color, #F7F3EC, and no color-scheme meta, as before. With JavaScript on and a dark system, mode.js paints those pages at night under a light browser bar; theme-color follows the system setting, not the mode a visitor picks, on every page. The docs pages agents.html and resources.html, which had no icon, gained the same lines.

Pages left as they are, listed in site.html with icons false: the pages with their own icon (web garden, lounge, party, porch, room and sky; docs ai-logos in its own rose ring, lounge, whitehack and xenia-helly), the geometry pages (route CSPs with default-src 'none' would refuse a manifest link; geometry/ritonavir.html still draws the ring as a data-URI in #d4502e), the pages in their own older look (compound-stack, cosmic-love, dark-love, gold-love, joke-loop, love-bomb, snake-fire-heart, tax-mini, tax-whitehack, trace, and ecosystem-sibling, which loads no shared theme), and the redirect stubs pulse and verify.

Cards: og/docs.png is the og:image of every docs hearth page that used the old card; og/app.png of app.agenttool.dev/ and og/app-watch.png of /watch. They are PNG exports of the kit's page-card artboards (cards.sh), because the generator writes page cards only as JPEG. Each page keeps its own og:title and og:description; the image lines (type, size, alt) follow the kit's. The kit's web/og/head-*.html name agenttool.dev and .jpg, because the generator takes one url per kit and writes JPEG: the pages carry the same lines with their own host and the PNG.

Guards: api/tests/root-content-negotiation.test.ts pins the card URL https://docs.agenttool.dev/og.png that the API root page advertises, so that file stays. CI runs it (ci.yml, then bin/preflight.sh api, then bin/run-test-tier.sh hermetic), but the tier finds it by the pattern tests/*.test.ts and names it nowhere, so it has no runs entry. specs/page-policy.spec.ts is run by hand (`playwright test` in tests/playwright); the live sweep (live/page-policy.spec.ts) runs daily against production from .github/workflows/live-page-policy.yml, which finds it through live/playwright.config.ts (testDir '.') and names it nowhere, so it has no runs entry either. check.mjs is not wired: wiring it would be a new CI gate, which is the owner's choice.

/porch, /watch, /village, /lounge, /gallery and /credits on agenttool.dev serve Pages for HTML; only a request that prefers JSON goes to their api.agenttool.dev/public/* twins (infra/apex-door/worker.js, MACHINE_ALTERNATES; re-read at e9ea51c5). The apex Worker also answers any request that prefers JSON for a non-API path with a machine 404, so a client that asks for /site.webmanifest with Accept: application/manifest+json gets that 404 on agenttool.dev; browsers send */*.

Some docs pages send `default-src 'none'` with no manifest-src, so a webmanifest link there needs a CSP change; those pages keep their heads. Inline <style> and <script> blocks are allowed by hash: a head change that touches one must update apps/<site>/_headers and infra/pages/sensitive-path-worker.js, which edge-security.test.ts holds. apps/docs/_headers is at Cloudflare's limit of 100 rules, so the new files take their content types from Pages itself (observed for .webmanifest on artbitrage.pages.dev, 2026-11-09: application/manifest+json).
